p.src: The Pilgrim was absorbed in watching the spectacle and failed to notice the flying sand and ash enter his nose. It tickled so badly that he sneezed twice. He turned around at once, felt beneath a crag for two pebbles, and plugged his nostrils with them. Shaking himself, he changed into a fire-gathering sparrowhawk and flew into the midst of the smoke and flames. After darting through them several times, he found that the sand and ash had vanished and the smoke and fire had subsided. He hurriedly resumed his true form and descended. Looking again, he heard the ding-dong clang of a bronze gong. He said to himself, “I must have taken the wrong road. This is not where the fiend lives. That gong sounds like the gong of a relay courier. This must be a highway through the kingdom, and some courier is carrying official dispatches. Old Sun had better go and question him.”

p.src: As he went on, he suddenly saw what appeared to be a little fiend hurrying toward him as if in flight, carrying a yellow flag on a shoulder pole, bearing dispatches on his back, and beating a gong. The Pilgrim laughed. “So it was this scoundrel beating the gong. I wonder what sort of message he is carrying. Let me listen to him.” Splendid Great Sage! He shook himself, changed into a gadfly, and lightly alighted upon the fiend’s dispatch bag. He heard the fiend beating his gong and muttering noisily to himself, “Our king is far too cruel-hearted. Three years ago he went to the Kingdom of Scarlet-Purple and carried off Queen Golden Sage by force. Yet all this time fate has denied him, and he has never been able to touch her; only the palace maids brought to him have suffered in her place. When two were brought, he tormented them to death; when four were brought, he tormented them to death as well. He demanded more the year before last, again last year, and again this year—and now he is demanding still more. But now he has met his match. The vanguard sent to demand the palace maids was defeated by someone called Sun the Pilgrim, and no maids were handed over. Our king was enraged by this and means to wage war against that kingdom, so he has ordered me to deliver some sort of challenge. On this errand, all will be well if that king refuses to fight; but if he fights, he is certain to fare badly. Once our king unleashes his smoke, fire, flying sand, neither that king nor his ministers nor any of his people can hope to survive. Then we shall seize their city; our king will proclaim himself emperor, and we shall become his ministers. Though we may all receive offices high or low, Heaven’s justice will never tolerate it.”

p.src: Rounding a mountain slope, he met the little monster and saluted him with folded hands. “Officer, where are you going? What official dispatch are you carrying?” The creature behaved as though he knew him. He stopped beating his gong, returned the salute with a cheerful smile, and said, “My king has sent me to deliver a declaration of war to the Kingdom of Scarlet and Purple.” The Pilgrim promptly asked, “Has that woman from the Kingdom of Scarlet and Purple ever coupled with your king?” The little monster said, “When she was abducted the year before last, an immortal immediately presented Queen Golden Sage with a five-colored celestial robe for her new attire. From the moment she put on that robe, needle-like spikes grew all over her body, and our king has not dared so much as touch her. If he merely takes hold of her a little, his palms begin to ache. No one knows why. From then until now, he has never touched her. This morning he sent the vanguard to demand palace maids to wait upon her, but some fellow called Sun the Pilgrim defeated him. Our king flew into a rage, so he ordered me to deliver this declaration of war and tell the Pilgrim to fight him tomorrow.” The Pilgrim asked, “Why is your king so vexed?” The little monster replied, “He is still there fuming now. Go and sing him a Daoist ballad to relieve his boredom.”

p.src: Our fine Pilgrim folded his hands, took his leave, and went away. The monster resumed beating his gong and continued on his way. Then the Pilgrim turned fierce. Drawing his staff, he wheeled around and struck the little monster once on the back of the head. Pitiful creature! His skull was smashed, blood and brains gushed out, his skin split, his neck broke, and his life ended. After putting away his staff, he regretted his haste. “I was a little too quick and forgot to ask his name. Never mind.” He removed the declaration of war from the corpse and hid it in his sleeve. He concealed the yellow banner and bronze gong in the grass beside the road. As he seized the corpse by the feet and was about to fling it into the ravine, he heard a clang, and a gold-inlaid identification plaque appeared at its waist. Words on the plaque read: “One trusted junior officer, named Comes and Goes. Short of stature, with a pockmarked face and no beard. To be worn at all times; anyone without the plaque is an impostor.” The Pilgrim laughed. “This wretch is named Comes and Goes, but that blow has made him go and never come back!” He untied the plaque and fastened it around his own waist. He was about to throw down the corpse when he recalled the deadly smoke and fire. For the moment he dared not seek the monster’s cave. Instead, he raised his staff, thrust it into the little monster’s chest, hoisted the body into the air, and went straight back to the kingdom to claim this as his first victory. See how, thinking the matter over as he went, he gave a whistle and arrived at the kingdom’s border.

p.src: The Pilgrim stepped forward, gave a salutation, and said, “Accept my greeting.” The lady said, “What an insolent, boorish monster! When I shared splendor and honor with the king in the Kingdom of Scarlet-Purple, even the grand preceptor and the chancellor would prostrate themselves in the dust at the sight of me, not daring to look up. How dare this wild monster tell me to ‘accept his greeting’? Where did such a rude boor come from?” The waiting women came forward and said, “My lady, please calm your anger. He is a trusted junior officer of His Majesty, named Coming-and-Going. He was the one sent to deliver the letter of challenge this morning.” Hearing this, the lady suppressed her anger and asked, “When you delivered the letter of challenge, did you reach the borders of the Kingdom of Scarlet-Purple?” The Pilgrim replied, “I carried the letter straight into the city and went to the Golden Throne Hall, where I met the sovereign face to face and obtained his reply.” The lady asked, “When you met the sovereign, what did he say?” The Pilgrim said, “I have just told His Majesty what the sovereign said about fighting and how he would deploy his troops and arrange his battle lines. But the sovereign misses you, my lady, and entrusted me with one message that will please your heart, which I came especially to report. Unfortunately, with so many people around us, this is no place to speak of it.”

p.src: On hearing this, the lady ordered the two ranks of foxes and deer to withdraw. The Pilgrim closed the palace doors, wiped his face, and revealed his true appearance. He said to the lady, “Do not be afraid of me. I am a monk sent from the Great Tang in the Eastern Land to the Great Western Heaven, to the Kingdom of India, there to visit the Buddha at the Thunderclap Monastery and seek the scriptures. My master is Tang Sanzang, the Tang emperor’s sworn younger brother. I am his chief disciple, Sun Wukong. When we passed through your kingdom to exchange our travel document, I saw that your sovereign and ministers had posted notices seeking a physician. Drawing on my considerable experience, I cured him of the illness caused by longing for you, and he held a banquet to thank me. While we were drinking, he told me how you had been abducted by the demon. Because I can subdue dragons and tame tigers, he especially asked me to capture the monster and rescue you so that you might return home. I was the vanguard who appeared to be defeated, and I was also the one who killed the lesser demon. When I saw how savage the guards outside his gate were, I transformed myself into Coming-and-Going and risked my life to enter this place and bring you word.” After hearing this, the lady pondered in silence. The Pilgrim took out the precious bracelet, presented it with both hands, and said, “If you do not believe me, look at this and tell me where else it could have come from.” The moment she saw it, tears streamed from her eyes. Descending from her seat, she bowed in gratitude and said, “Venerable elder, if you can truly rescue me and restore me to the court, I shall never forget your great kindness as long as I live.”

p.src: The Pilgrim said, “First let me ask you: what is that treasure of his that releases fire, smoke, and sand?” The lady replied, “It is hardly any great treasure, only three golden bells. When he shakes the first one, it sends out three hundred fathoms of flame to burn people; when he shakes the second, it sends out three hundred fathoms of smoke to choke people; and when he shakes the third, it sends out three hundred fathoms of yellow sand to blind and bewilder them. The smoke and fire are not so serious, but the yellow sand is deadly. If it enters a person’s nostrils, it will cost him his life.” The Pilgrim said, “Formidable indeed! Formidable indeed! I have encountered it myself, and it made me sneeze twice. But where does he keep those bells?” The lady replied, “He would never put them down. He wears them at his waist, and whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, they never leave his person.” The Pilgrim said, “If your heart still belongs to the Kingdom of Scarlet-Purple and you wish to be reunited with the king, then put aside your grief and sorrow for the time being. Assume a charming and joyful expression, show him some affection as a wife, and persuade him to entrust the bells to your keeping. I shall seize an opportunity to steal them and subdue the demon. Then I can take you home, where you and the king may be joined once more like phoenix and mate and live together in peace.” The lady agreed to do as he said.

The lady ordered, “Youlai-Youqu, hurry to the front pavilion and invite your king here so that I may speak with him.” Dear Wukong answered at once, went straight to the Flaying Pavilion, and told the fiend, “Your Majesty, the lady of the sacred palace requests your presence.” The demon king said delightedly, “The lady usually does nothing but scold me. Why has she invited me today?” Wukong replied, “The lady asked about the king of Zhuzi, so I told her, ‘He no longer wants you; his realm has installed another empress.’ On hearing this, the lady abandoned all hope of him and only then sent me to invite you.” The demon king was overjoyed. “You have indeed proved useful. Once I have destroyed his kingdom, I shall appoint you grand chancellor at my court.”

p.src: Wukong readily thanked him for the favor and hurried with the demon king to the rear palace gate. The lady greeted him with a cheerful face and reached out to take his hand. Murmuring deferentially, the demon king drew back and said, “I dare not, I dare not. I am deeply grateful for Your Ladyship’s affection, but I fear the pain in my hands and dare not come close.” The lady said, “Please be seated, Your Majesty. I have something to tell you.” The demon king replied, “Say whatever you wish.” The lady said, “For three years now I have been subjected to Your Majesty’s unworthy affection, yet we have never shared pillow or quilt. It must have been a bond from a former life that made us husband and wife. Yet who would have thought that Your Majesty meant to keep me at a distance and would not treat me as a wife? I remember that when I was empress in the kingdom of Zhuzi, whenever a foreign land offered some treasure as tribute, the sovereign would inspect it and invariably give it to his empress for safekeeping. Here you have no treasures at all: those around you wear sable furs and eat bloody meat, and I have never once seen silk brocade, gold, or pearls. There are only hides spread beneath us and rugs laid over us. Or perhaps you do possess some treasures, but because you regard me as an outsider, you neither let me see them nor entrust them to my care. For instance, I hear that you have three bells, which I suppose must be treasures. Why do you carry them wherever you go and even while you sit? You could give them to me for safekeeping and take them out whenever you need them; there would be no harm in that. Since we are husband and wife, this too would show that you trust me with your innermost affairs. If you will not place such trust in me, what is that but treating me as an outsider?” The demon king laughed heartily and apologized. “Your Ladyship is right to reproach me, quite right. The treasures are here, and today I shall entrust them to your keeping.” With that, he lifted his clothes to take out the treasures. Standing nearby, Wukong watched without blinking as the monster lifted two or three layers of clothing, revealing three bells worn close against his body. He untied them, plugged their mouths with cotton, wrapped them into a bundle in a piece of leopard skin, and handed them to the lady, saying, “Though these objects are humble, you must store them with great care. On no account must you shake them.” Taking the bundle, the lady said, “I understand. I shall set it upon this dressing table, where no one will disturb it.” Then she called, “Servants, prepare wine! The king and I shall celebrate our happy reconciliation with a few cups.” Hearing her command, the maids at once laid out fruits and vegetables, set down meat from roe deer, muntjac, deer, and rabbit, and poured coconut wine to serve them. The lady assumed a seductive manner to beguile the fiend.

p.src: Sun Wukong, watching for his chance nearby, edged and felt his way toward the dressing table, gently picked up the three golden bells, then crept slowly out through the palace gate and made straight away from the cave dwelling. Reaching a deserted spot before the Flaying Pavilion, he opened the leopard-skin wrapper and looked. The middle bell was as large as a teacup, while the two on either side were each as large as a fist. Not knowing how dangerous they were, he pulled out the cotton. He heard only a bright clang, and smoke, fire, and yellow sand came bursting out in a roaring torrent. Unable to stop them in time, he soon had the whole pavilion blazing fiercely. Terrified, the gatekeeping fiends rushed together into the rear palace and alarmed the demon king, who hastily ordered, “Put out the fire! Put out the fire!” When he came out to look, he discovered that Youlai-Youqu had taken the golden bells. The demon king strode forward and shouted, “You vile slave! How dare you steal my precious golden bells and play your tricks with them here?” “Give them here! Give them here!” he cried. At the gate, the Tiger General, Bear Marshal, Leopard Head, Tiger-Cat Commander, Otter-Elephant, Grey Wolf, Docile Roe, Cunning Hare, Long Serpent, Great Python, and Orangutan led all the fiends in closing around him.

p.src: Caught in a panic, Wukong dropped the golden bells, resumed his true form, drew out his As-You-Will Gold-Banded Staff, and, displaying all his skill, struck wildly before him. The demon king recovered his treasures and issued an order: “Shut the front gate!” Hearing him, the fiends set about their tasks: some shut the gate while others joined the fight. Finding escape difficult, Wukong put away his staff, shook himself, and changed into a foolish little bluebottle fly, which clung to a bare stone wall untouched by the flames. Unable to find him, the fiends reported, “Your Majesty, the thief has escaped! The thief has escaped!” The demon king asked, “Did he go out through the gate?” The fiends all replied, “The front gate is still tightly locked and securely barred. He did not get out.” The demon king merely said, “Search carefully.” Some fetched water to douse the fire while others searched with care, but they found no trace of him. The demon king said angrily, “What manner of thief was he? How audacious—to assume Youlai-Youqu’s appearance, come in and make his report to me, then stay by my side and seize the chance to steal my treasures! Fortunately, he did not manage to carry them outside. Had he taken them beyond the mountain and exposed them to the wind of heaven, what would we have done?” The Tiger General stepped forward and said, “Your Majesty’s vast good fortune reaches heaven, and our allotted span is not yet exhausted; that is why we discovered him in time.” The Bear Marshal stepped forward and said, “Your Majesty, that thief was none other than Sun Wukong, the one who defeated our vanguard. He must have encountered Youlai-Youqu on the road, killed him, seized his yellow flag, bronze gong, and ivory tally, and then assumed his appearance to come here and deceive Your Majesty.” The demon king said, “Exactly, exactly. That reasoning is sound.” Then he called, “Servants, search carefully and keep strict guard. Do not open the gate and let him escape!” And so the situation promised that:
